newsitem.title: UK: IPE May Brent trades lower before expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE May Brent trades lower before expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent futures continued to trade lower on Tuesday after NYMEX opened but were off earlier lows, with reports of some selling and positive sentiment that Iran was trying to defuse its latest crisis with the United States.
The May Brent contract, which expires at the end of Tuesday's session, was trading 18 cents a barrel down at $18.01 by 1513 GMT after trading within a range of 22-26 cents down after NYMEX opened.
The June contract was down one cent at $18.33 after being eight cents down at $18.26 earlier.
Brokers said there was some selling in the market, with at least one player appearing to have sold some 2,500 lots of the Brent June contract, trying to push it down.
One broker said that besides the reports of selling, the market was also pushed down by sentiment that tension between Iran and the West was easing.

The market moved up on Monday partly on a weekend report in the Washington Post, attributed to U.S. and Arab officials, linking a senior Iranian government official to a group of Shi'ite Moslems suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year.

Brokers said the market was now keenly awaiting the latest American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly data due out after the market closes on Tuesday. Last week's report showed that in the week ended April 4, U.S. crude oil stocks rose to 309.95 million barrels.
IPE gas oil reversed its earlier losses, with the May contract trading $1 higher at $166 at 1504 GMT. It later eased back to $165.50 a tonne. -- Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
